newsitem.title: CHINA: China says price gap behind copper shipments.
newsitem.headline: China says price gap behind copper shipments.

text.p: China's planned delivery of up to 10,000 tonnes of copper to Singapore warehouses is the result of low domestic prices and not an attempt to flood the world market, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

China should export up to 50,000 tonnes of copper to help to balance a domestic market hit by heavy imports and restrained demand, the newspaper quoted an official of the China Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp as saying.
The newspaper gave no timescale for the suggested exports.

It dismissed suggestions from traders that the delivery of 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of copper to London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses in Singapore, announced in June, was a ploy to drive down international prices and allow future purchases.
At 23,000 yuan ($2,770) a tonne, the price of domestic copper was well below the 27,000 yuan final price tag on imported copper, a gap that had prompted the exports, it said.
